title: Smooth vs Rough Surfaces
description: Why can you see your face in a mirror but not in a wall — even though both reflect light? Anaya is puzzled. Solve it to earn the next crystal shard.

content.value: Both a mirror and a wall reflect light — and both obey the laws of reflection at every point. The difference is the SURFACE. A smooth surface gives a clear image; a rough surface does not.

On a very smooth surface (a mirror, still water, polished metal), parallel rays of light bounce off staying parallel. Because they stay neat and organised, they form a clear image. This is called REGULAR reflection.

On a rough surface (a wall, paper, wood), the tiny bumps face in all directions. Parallel rays hit the bumps and scatter in many directions. No clear image forms. This is called DIFFUSED or irregular reflection. Importantly, the laws of reflection are STILL obeyed at each tiny point — the surface is just uneven.

REGULAR (smooth)          DIFFUSED (rough)
 ||||  →  ||||             |||| →  / | \ \ /
 parallel stays parallel   rays scatter everywhere
 = clear image             = no clear image
Diffused reflection is why we can see non-luminous objects like walls, books and faces from every direction — scattered light reaches our eyes no matter where we stand.
Key Takeaway: Smooth surfaces give regular reflection (clear image); rough surfaces give diffused reflection (scattered light, no image). The laws of reflection hold in both cases.

quiz.question: Why does a wall NOT show your reflection like a mirror does?
options: Walls do not reflect any light
The rough wall scatters light in all directions (diffused reflection)
The laws of reflection do not work on walls
quiz.explain: A rough wall scatters parallel rays in many directions, so no clear image forms — that is diffused reflection.

quiz.question: On a smooth mirror, parallel incident rays reflect as…
options: parallel rays, forming a clear image
rays that stop at the surface
quiz.explain: A smooth surface keeps parallel rays parallel, producing regular reflection and a clear image.

quiz.question: In diffused reflection, the laws of reflection are…
options: still obeyed at every point on the rough surface
quiz.explain: Each tiny point of a rough surface still obeys i = r. The surface is just uneven, so the rays scatter.
